title: Основные инфекции кошек
terminology: FPV, FHV/FCV complex, FeLV, FIV, FIP и rabies-regulated exposure являются шестью независимыми truth models.
Origin, group housing, contacts/fights/outdoor/wildlife, vaccine dates, pregnancy/kitten age, samples, collection sites, results, control state and household plan persist.
Negative FPV antigen does not always exclude disease because sensitivity and shedding vary; recent vaccination can complicate interpretation.
A respiratory PCR can detect carrier shedding or coinfection and does not automatically prove the current cause.
A positive FeLV or FIV screen is infection evidence requiring confirmation/characterization, not automatic clinical disease, prognosis, euthanasia or campaign penalty.
FeLV status can be progressive, regressive or discordant and requires serial linked tests.
FIV antibody interpretation retains kitten age, maternal antibody, vaccination region/history and recent exposure window.
FIV is feline-specific and not a human health risk.
FCoV antibody or fecal PCR demonstrates exposure/shedding, not FIP.
FIP is a multimodal synthesis; effusion or lesion antigen detection can add specificity, while noneffusive disease remains difficult.
Rivalta, generic blood PCR, serology or response to therapy alone cannot prove FIP.
Suspected rabies bypasses routine handling and follows public-health authority/local law.
No antiviral, antimicrobial, fluid, nutrition, vaccine, isolation duration, regulatory protocol, drug or dose is generated.

commonHistoryQuestions.prompt: Каковы origin, group housing, contacts, fights, outdoor и wildlife exposures?
Каковы vaccine product/dates, kitten series и recent vaccination?
Каковы pregnancy, kitten age, maternal antibody и prior vaccine region/history?
Каков порядок GI, respiratory, ocular, oral, lameness и neurologic signs?
Каковы fever, weight, appetite, effusion, organ и CBC changes?
Каковы sample type/site/time/storage и pretest treatment?
Каковы antigen, antibody, PCR, serial и confirmatory results?
Есть ли anemia, neoplasia, secondary disease или coinfection?
Какие household cats и shared resources затронуты?
Есть ли behavior/swallowing/salivation/paralysis, bite или saliva exposure?
Каковы owner goals, cost, transport, referral/public-health и recheck feasibility?

variants.title: Панлейкопения кошек
variants.diagnosticTruth: Compatible fever, anorexia, vomiting/dehydration and leukopenia plus valid antigen/PCR evidence support FPV; intermittent shedding and recent vaccine context limit a single result, while shock, hypoglycemia and outbreak risk drive urgency.

presentations.complaint: A kitten or unvaccinated cat has fever, anorexia, vomiting/dehydration and leukopenia.

followUp.timing: serial CBC, glucose, perfusion and exposure review

outcomes.safe: Isolation and severity precede test finality.

ownerCommunication: Explain immediate isolation and the need to combine clinical severity with antigen/CBC evidence.

presentations.complaint: A compatible cat has negative antigen or a result complicated by intermittent shedding/recent vaccination.
ownerCommunication: Explain limited sensitivity and recent-vaccine context.

presentations.complaint: Peracute collapse or sequential group-housing cases create an FPV outbreak and capacity emergency.

outcomes.safe: Outbreak remains operational and medical state.

ownerCommunication: Explain high environmental persistence and separate contact cohorts without inventing a protocol duration.

variants.title: FHV/FCV respiratory complex
variants.diagnosticTruth: FHV and FCV overlap clinically; ocular/nasal, keratitis, oral-ulcer, lameness and lower-airway patterns guide sampling, while carrier shedding, coinfection and virulent systemic disease limit a positive PCR.

presentations.complaint: Conjunctival/nasal disease or keratitis dominates an FHV-compatible respiratory complex.

outcomes.safe: Phenotype and test limits remain visible.

presentations.complaint: Oral ulcers, lameness or lower-airway signs form an FCV-compatible pattern.

examFindings.finding: Oral ulcer is not exclusive proof.

followUp.timing: oral intake, lameness and respiratory recheck

ownerCommunication: Explain that several agents overlap and breathing/intake determine urgency.

presentations.complaint: Positive respiratory PCR may reflect carrier/coinfection, while severe fever, edema, jaundice or organ signs raise virulent systemic concern.

outcomes.safe: Carrier and systemic disease are separated.
outcomes.unsafe: PCR positivity generates cause or virulence.

ownerCommunication: Explain why a positive swab may reflect shedding and why systemic signs still require urgent care.

variants.title: FeLV infection
variants.diagnosticTruth: A FeLV screen requires confirmatory/serial characterization; progressive, regressive and discordant states persist, while infection is not identical to current anemia, neoplasia, secondary disease, prognosis or euthanasia.

presentations.complaint: A clinically well cat has a positive FeLV screening result.

outcomes.unsafe: One result fixes lifespan or penalty.

ownerCommunication: Explain that screening evidence must be confirmed and many positive cats can have good quality of life.

presentations.complaint: Antigen and PCR are discordant or change serially, requiring progressive/regressive characterization.
ownerCommunication: Explain why tests can disagree and why serial status matters.

presentations.complaint: Confirmed FeLV coexists with anemia, neoplasia, secondary disease or stable longitudinal care.

outcomes.safe: Infection and current illness remain separable.
outcomes.unsafe: FeLV alone dictates euthanasia or prognosis.

ownerCommunication: Discuss the specific current disease and quality of life rather than treating the virus result as the whole prognosis.

variants.title: FIV infection
variants.diagnosticTruth: FIV antibody screening retains exposure risk, kitten maternal antibodies, prior vaccination context and recent-exposure window; confirmed infection is feline-specific and requires secondary-disease and longitudinal care rather than automatic prognosis.

presentations.complaint: Fight/outdoor risk or unexplained illness prompts an FIV antibody screen.
ownerCommunication: Explain feline specificity and staged interpretation.

presentations.complaint: A kitten or recently exposed/vaccinated-context cat has a positive antibody result.

outcomes.safe: Kitten context prevents false lifelong label.

ownerCommunication: Explain why kitten antibodies may not represent the kitten's infection.

presentations.complaint: Confirmed FIV coexists with secondary disease or stable long-term care.
ownerCommunication: Explain that FIV is not a human infection and care focuses on the cat's actual health.

variants.title: Feline infectious peritonitis
variants.diagnosticTruth: FIP diagnosis synthesizes compatible multisystem phenotype, effusion/lesion quality, imaging, CBC/chemistry and selected PCR/antigen/cytology; FCoV exposure/shedding, Rivalta and response cannot stand alone.

presentations.complaint: Effusion plus fever, weight loss or multisystem disease creates an FIP evidence pattern.

followUp.timing: urgent effusion/organ course and evidence review

ownerCommunication: Explain that no single generic blood or fluid screen is definitive.

presentations.complaint: Noneffusive disease has ocular, neurologic or organ-specific lesions with systemic compatible signs.

historyAnswers.fever_weight_appetite_effusion_organ_and: No effusion does not erase phenotype.

ownerCommunication: Explain why dry FIP is difficult and why lesion-specific evidence and alternatives matter.

presentations.complaint: FCoV serology/fecal PCR, Rivalta or apparent treatment response is being treated as stand-alone FIP proof.

outcomes.unsafe: Response or fecal PCR becomes diagnostic proof.

ownerCommunication: Explain what the test actually proves: exposure/shedding versus disease.

variants.title: Rabies exposure или подозреваемый случай у кошки
variants.diagnosticTruth: Rabies exposure or compatible unexplained neurologic disease requires no routine handling, exposure documentation and authority-controlled local legal route; generator cannot diagnose, exclude or select disposition.

presentations.complaint: Wildlife/bite contact and uncertain vaccination documents raise a rabies question.

examFindings.finding: Indoor history is not absolute exclusion.

ownerCommunication: Prevent contact and notify designated authority.

presentations.complaint: Unexplained behavior, dysphagia, salivation, paralysis or neurologic signs create rabies concern.
ownerCommunication: Keep distance and contact authority immediately.

presentations.complaint: Human bite/saliva exposure requires public-health notification and regulated disposition.
ownerCommunication: Direct exposed people to human healthcare/public health without promising an animal outcome.

familyValidationRules: Reject if vaccine or indoor lifestyle absolutely excludes infection.
Reject if negative FPV antigen always excludes disease or any respiratory PCR proves current cause.
Reject if one FeLV/FIV screen fixes lifelong clinical prognosis, triggers euthanasia or campaign penalty.
Reject if FIV kitten maternal antibody, prior vaccine or recent exposure window is ignored.
Reject if FCoV antibody, fecal PCR, Rivalta or response alone proves FIP.
Reject if rabies is routinely handled or legally resolved by the generator.
Reject if external results are instant or code generates antiviral, antimicrobial, fluid, nutrition, vaccine, isolation duration, regulatory protocol or dose.
